_comment: The contract for path forwarding, shared by two implementations that must never disagree:
the Go route builder (internal/proxy/caddy/routes.go), which renders the Caddy handlers that
actually rewrite the request, and the TypeScript preview (lib/domain-path.ts), which tells the
operator what those handlers will do before they save.
Nothing else keeps them in step. If the preview drifts from the builder it does not fail, it
lies — and a preview that confidently shows the wrong answer is worse than no preview at all.
Every `expected` value below was observed against a real Caddy, proxying to an upstream that
echoes back the URI it received. They are not derived from either implementation.

cases.name: strip only — the app does not know it is behind a prefix
path without strip — the app expects to be mounted under the prefix
internal path only — the app insists on its own base path (Grafana under /gf)
strip then prepend — a genuine remap (Dokploy's own documented example)
the app's own root, stripped, is / and not the empty string
internal path on the app's own root keeps the trailing slash Caddy produces
